PROVENANCE — real coach records from a real build; DO NOT hand-edit.

What these four files are
  Byte-for-byte copies of the four records the coach wrote on TASK-8388-001,
  a feature task of build-FEAT-8388 on the api_test repository, on
  6 September 2026. api_test keeps its database schema in Alembic migrations
  (alembic/env.py, alembic/versions/). TASK-8388-001 is the task that added
  the "domain" column to the users model. These are the records of its two
  turns: the turn that added the column and was sent back, and the turn that
  changed nothing and was approved.

Where they came from (read-only copy, taken 2026-09-06)
  /home/richardwoollcott/forge-state/receipts/build-FEAT-8388-20260906180545/
    .guardkit/autobuild-private/TASK-8388-001/coach_turn_1.json

    .guardkit/autobuild-private/TASK-8388-001/coach_turn_2.json
    .guardkit/autobuild-private/TASK-8388-001/coach_evidence_turn_2.json

What happened on the build
  (From autobuild-stdout.log in the receipts directory above; the line
  numbers are that file's.)

  Turn 1. The Player changed three files (line 210: "turn 1 changed 3
  file(s) in the worktree (git-measured)"): src/users/models.py (the
  "domain" column), src/users/schemas.py, and a new
  tests/users/test_user_domain.py. No Alembic migration. The coach sent the
  turn back (line 250: "Coach provided feedback on turn 1") for a reason
  that had nothing to do with the database: the verification run could not
  collect or run any tests, which the coach reads as absent evidence, not a
  pass. That is what coach_turn_1.json says (a major finding that the
  evidence gathering aborted, and a should_fix note that the missing test
  signal is not a signal about the code), and coach_evidence_turn_1.json
  records the gathering as "partial_gate_abort" with no independent-test
  result at all. The build checkpoints every completed turn, feedback turns
  included, so the three files were committed anyway, as fcb67c59 (line
  249: "Checkpoint created: fcb67c59 for turn 1"). From then on the
  unmigrated model change was in HEAD.

  Turn 2. The Player changed nothing (line 342: "turn 2 changed 0 file(s)
  in the worktree (git-measured)"). The independent test run now collected
  and passed 15 tests, and the behavioural oracle ran and passed — but the
  oracle was testing a Docker image built on 25 July, not this build's code
  (coach_evidence_turn_2.json records both results). The coach approved
  (line 510: "Coach approved on turn 2") with three should_fix honesty
  notes, one for each file the Player listed but had not touched on this
  turn — those files were already in the turn-1 checkpoint. The turn was
  checkpointed as 197d3a5b (line 513).

  TASK-8388-002 then ran one turn that also changed nothing (line 713:
  "turn 1 changed 0 file(s)") and was approved, and the build went through.
  The unit tests could not see the gap at any point: they build the schema
  from the model.

  The deploy into the Docker Sandbox then found it: on a freshly created
  database, built by running the migrations, the users table had no
  "domain" column. 44 checks passed and 6 failed, and the candidate was
  refused.

Why the guard reads the feature's base commit, not HEAD
  On this path a check that reads the worktree's difference from HEAD sees
  the three files on turn 1 (a verdict already sent back; the guard only
  overrides an approval) and nothing on turn 2, whose tree was clean. So
  AgentInvoker._apply_schema_change_without_migration_guard reads the
  worktree's difference from the feature's base commit — the commit the
  feature's worktree was created from — resolved the way guardkit's own
  seam checks resolve it (seam_checks.resolve_feature_base: the recorded
  .guardkit/autobuild/<feature>/feature_base.json, else git merge-base
  HEAD main). Against that base, the column committed by the turn-1
  checkpoint is still an added line on turn 2, and a migration added by an
  earlier turn or an earlier task of the same feature is still seen.

How the tests use them
  coach_turn_2.json is the real approval that let the unmigrated model
  through: the verdict the guard flips to feedback, with the coach's three
  notes kept behind the guard's one must_fix issue.

  coach_evidence_turn_2.json is that turn's real evidence bundle, threaded
  through the real invoke_coach path so the whole override chain runs.

  coach_turn_1.json is the real feedback verdict from the turn that added
  the column. The guard never touches a feedback verdict; the test says so
  with this record.

  coach_evidence_turn_1.json is that turn's evidence — gathering aborted,
  no independent-test result — the shape of absent evidence, which is
  never read as a defect.

  The worktree shape the guard reads — the model line added since the
  feature's base commit and nothing added under alembic/versions/ — is
  built by the tests in a temporary git repository, both as an uncommitted
  change and as a committed "checkpoint" behind a recorded feature base,
  which is this build's real sequence.

No secrets: all four files were scanned for API keys, passwords, tokens and
message-broker URLs before they were copied (zero matches).
